name: wyrd-mcp
description: wyrd — an MCP server that exposes one granted folder to any AI client, read-only, behind a path-containment fence with documented limits.
//exports: ⚠⚠ EMPTY ON PURPOSE, AND IT IS A DECLARATION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. This package is a BINARY. Until 2026-08-31 it declared `bin` and no `exports`, which does not mean 'nothing is importable' — it means EVERYTHING under `files` is: `dist/main.js`, `dist/server.js`, `dist/index.js` and `dist/fsgate.js` were all deep-importable by any consumer, and this project's own rule (stated in the fence source and in E12's failure message) is that shipping `dist` makes it public. An empty map closes the whole class instead of one member, so the next refactor does not reopen the same fork. ⚠ `bin` is UNAFFECTED: npm links the binary by filesystem path and Node executes it by path, and `exports` gates only bare-specifier resolution. ⚠ The fence is not hidden by this — it moved to `wyrd-fence`, where it is a first-class declared entry point with a versioned type surface. That is the opposite of a compatibility facade and must not be softened back into one.
//dependencies: ⚠ `wyrd-fence` IS AN EXACT REGISTRY VERSION, NEVER `workspace:*` OR `file:`. npm links the matching local workspace package automatically, so the exact version is what a stranger's install resolves AND what this machine builds against — one spec, both regimes. ⚠ AND THE PUBLISH ORDER IS FORCED: `wyrd-fence@<this version>` must exist on the registry BEFORE this package is published, or every stranger's install fails at resolution while every gate here stays green. `scripts/run-tests.mjs` asserts the three declared versions agree with the fence's own, and `scripts/publish-prerequisites.mjs` — reached from `scripts/release-publish.mjs` — is the gate that asserts the registry actually has it before this package goes out. That gate said 'not yet, it belongs to the publish slice' until 2026-09-01; the publish slice landed it.
